name: gpac
desc: Multimedia framework for research and academic purposes
why: A research multimedia framework that dissects containers and streaming protocols like MP4 and DASH, a real door into how media is structured.

brief.what_it_is: GPAC is an open-source multimedia framework written in C, with a library (libgpac) and command-line tools. It can process, analyse, package, stream, encode, decode and play back audio, video, subtitles, metadata, encrypted media, 2D/3D graphics and ECMAScript. Media goes in as files, pipes, sockets, HTTP or capture devices, and comes out as remuxed or segmented files, streams, or playback. Its best-known tool is MP4Box, a command-line MP4 manipulator for importing and extracting media, inspecting files, DASH segmentation and RTP hinting. The gpac command is a direct interface to its filter engine, which lets you chain any combination of filters. The project also ships MP4Box.js, a JavaScript library for parsing and writing MP4 in browsers and Node.js.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents GPAC as a standards-focused framework for processing, inspecting, packaging, streaming and playing media, aimed at video enthusiasts, academic researchers, standardization bodies and professional broadcasters. Its own description says it is best known for its MP4/ISOBMFF capabilities. The 2025 MP4Box.js post frames the project's core mission as giving developers high-quality, efficient, modular building blocks for multimedia workflows.
brief.how_it_works: Features are packaged as processing modules called filters, and the filter engine manages stream flow between them. The gpac application exposes that engine directly, so you can build a pipeline from any filters. MP4Box is a front end that uses the same engine, and most GPAC applications are built on it. The README says the tools are mostly wrappers around libgpac, which can be embedded in other projects.

brief.install_notes: Prebuilt stable and nightly installers for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS are on gpac.io/downloads. To compile it yourself, the README points to the build section of the wiki. The test suite lives in a separate repository, which you get by running git submodule update --init inside the GPAC checkout. The README also mentions Python and NodeJS bindings. No Homebrew-specific steps appeared in the pages I read.
brief.standout: The README describes GPAC as a filter graph engine, not just a converter, so MP4Box is one front end on top of a general pipeline system. The MP4Box.js library brings the same MP4 parsing and rewriting into browsers and Node, and its 1.0.0 release adds full MP4 rewriting including the mdat payload.
brief.status: Maintained. The GitHub README gives the current version as 26.08-DEV, and the homepage lists GPAC 26.07 as the latest release, dated 24 July 2026, with a 26.02 release before it. The homepage also has a 2024 post responding to CISA advisories, saying the project is actively patched. The README includes build and test badges and links to per-commit build results.
brief.caveats: Licensed under LGPL v2.1 or later, but most of it is also available under a commercial license from MotionSpell. The codebase is C and parses untrusted bitstreams, and CISA has issued advisories on it; the project's own 2024 post says those are mostly low to medium severity and already patched, but it is the project's own view. The README roadmap lists Web GUI, Rust and SWIG bindings, live JIT packaging, custom WASM filters, GnuTLS support and FFmpeg hardware acceleration as unchecked, so they are not done. Building from source is not described beyond a pointer to the wiki.
